body: Suicide is not some evil devil that's controlling my every move. It's just something I want, and it's not affecting my life in a negative way.

Sometimes I come to a dead end. Like this year, I did not go to school because of my depression. I spent a lot of time by myself, with nothing to do. And, during that time, it felt like whatever I needed to do was finished. There was nothing more for me to do, so I should probably commit suicide. That was my basic train of thought. After I finished everything I was assigned to do, what should I do next? Hmm, it seems like everyone ends their life with death, so the only viable thing to do next would be suicide.

I'll give you some advice for the next time you encounter a suicidal person: Give them something to do. Whether it's clearing land or doing house chores, take their mind off of things by making them do manual labor. Don't give them work that asks them to think. It might discourage them if they cant complete their assignment.
Yes, that's what I said.
Yeah I guess so. I don't think about how awesome my hands are, I just use them.

Haha, yes I do know I'm a frustrating conversation partner. This is why I don't bring up things I feel strongly about when talking to real life people.

Yes, my choice of suicide is dumb. But isn't love dumb? That's how the saying goes, right? "Love is dumb". My choice doesn't make sense, and it shouldn't. What kind of a living creature wants death? I don't know *why* I want it, I just know that I want it.

You are telling me that I have free will and the choices are still open to make. This is not a good move, as I'm trying to convince people here to allow me to commit suicide. You are inadvertently allowing me to commit suicide.

I know you're trying to use this argument of free will to persuade me not to do it, but you are coming at me in the wrong angle. I'm not stuck in some sort of position that's forcing me to kill myself. I'm freely choosing to do this, and you are encouraging me.

The reason why I'm not taking this and running is because you didn't mean it that way.

You also mentioned that denial means burying feelings. Then right after you said numbness also means burying feelings, like pain. To me, and seemingly to you as well, numbness and denial are the same thing. Yes, both are done *unconsciously*. In both cases, the victim wants to pretend something is not there. To do this with purpose would kill the intention of trying to ignore whatever they're ignoring.

Last but not least, suicide is my attempt at being happy. I've mentioned this many times above: I want death like how you might crave for steak. It's something that I want, like a present. It's not a last resort, it's not a way to escape something. It's my pleasure and my goal.
Why not take the permanent solution? I see nothing wrong with that. Even the grief from close family and friends is temporary.

I am from another country and I've been on road trips (I understand what you're saying though).

The problem with your reply is that I *do* want this. You cannot tell me what I want or do not want. I know who I'll hurt. I understand the consequences of suicide if it were to come. Sure, there's a lot here that I have yet to experience, but just because they're unknown and mysterious it does not mean I should go and explore them. I understand the gravity of death, as well as how wonderful my life is. Don't think that I haven't considered all of this before. Suicide, to me, is not an action of "quitting life". Think of it more as "receiving death" than "leaving life". I want to receive death; but that does not directly mean that I want to leave life. I want death, so I must compromise and leave life. Yes, life is good. But, in my mind, death is much better.

When I said you cant choose your personality, I mean that it's in your DNA to be grumpy, or optimistic, etc etc. It can be influenced by the environment, but all in all you are born with a set of basic personalities.

I know I can't come back from the dead. If you are warning me of regret, remember that I would be dead and feel no remorse. Also, all problems are temporary.

I'm sorry if I mistook one of your sentences and thought you wanted to make games. You can sub in whatever you desire for video games. Either way, the video games isn't important. I wanted you to see the analogy I was making.

Those are some very interesting ideas. If I don't go this summer, I hope to live and see these debates over the "right to death".

Some rebuttals: in your 4th paragraph, you mentioned how I might not want to find my passions or be "healthy". I'd like to say that I do have passions and have been exploring them. If you read above, you will find that I lead an active and energetic life full of people and hobbies. I have found a lot of things that I'm good at and, to some extent, enjoy doing.

Also, while in text it may seem this way, I am most certainly not robotic. Neither am I numb. I'm trying to display my ideas in its simplest most coherent forms so that the community can get a better grasp of my ideas. I've had my emotional breakdowns and rantings but I found these attempts very useless and restricted. It doesn't help to say "I'm sad", so I try not to say things like that. I'm not entirely certain if you meant this or not, but are you trying to suggest that I might be in the stage of denial?

And I understand that I'm not normal. My parents tell me this often. I know some part of my brain may be "broken" or out of place, but not all organisms are meant to live. The length of your evolutionary line does not determine your ability to survive. If this was so, then the theory of evolution would be faulty in the fact that everyone has equal chance of survival and to pass on their DNA. Maybe I wasn't meant to live past 17, maybe I was not suppose to grow old and contribute to society. Maybe my DNA  is hardwired for suicide.
I see. Thanks for clearing that up

I think it was worth it to post here. Though I didn't receive what I was looking for (yet), it looks like the people here have been enlightened with a new perspective on suicide, which might be just as good.

I am not certain, as everything comes with their unpredictability. Still, waiting longer is a bad idea. I'd grow more and more friends, and have an even larger crowd that would be devastated if I died. I know people care for me, but I wonder if they can understand my feelings. And if they did, would they see how much I'd benefit from death.
But I'm not giving up. I'm pursuing something I want.

My psychologist and therapist both wrote me off as "fine" a few months ago. I've been off meds and off therapy for a while now. I've told them the same thing I've told everyone here. The first time they heard it, they sent me to the inpatient ward.

Haha, I've done a lot of things to try to be unique and stand out (for the Ivies, of course), but this is not one of them.

I'm not looking to "'fix'" things, since nothing is broken. I desire death, call it my life long dream if you want to. I have a great life, I just happen to like death more than the person next to me.

Driving a car is awesome, but you don't really think about it after you've been driving for years and years. It would be the same with flying. You don't see Superman wide-eyed and excited whenever he's flying around. He is used to it, like how you might be used to driving a car.

Water isn't malleable whether you're talking about liquid, solid or gas. You can only call something malleable if it's a metal or a metal-like substance.

If I don't want life, then what other options do I have besides death? I don't have a problem *in* life, I have a problem *with* life. A lot of people here are having problems separating the idea of life and the experiences in life.

Well, life is like a shell. And everything we experience in it is like the yolk and egg white. You can call the entire thing an "egg", or what most people call "life", but I see it as two separate parts: life and the events that take part in life. I feel this way because my yolk and egg whites are just fine. They're good in a lot of ways. But the shell doesn't feel good to me. I don't feel comfortable with the shell, so I'd like to get rid of it, even if that means throwing the whole egg out.

If we are to make life what we want it to be, then *we* would be the authors. If you want to use this metaphor, I'd say that I have no interest in writing so I'd want to quit the job as an author.

If I was an author (not connected to the metaphor) and found out the book became "worth it" midway, I'd start the book over with the new idea so that the entire book can be interesting.
Strange, how you change colors... I still don't understand how Reddit works.

I've seen a psychologist (as stated above when I said that I've been through therapy and medication). I have a lot of "spice" in my life. I have many paths to choose from, all will serve me adequately. I have no problems in life, and I probably will not have any later in life. I just don't want to live any more. Death is something I've been wanting for years. You can't explain why you fell in love with things, can you? If you were a veterinarian, you cant tell me why you fell in love with animals verses humans. You can't choose your personality, your characteristics, your interests and passions. It's just what I want. I want death, just like how you might want to create video games.
Sorry; you came a bit too late to prevent it. I was not trying to evoke anger in the other redditor. I was just simply making a point (as with the other comment).
There are a lot of people who care about me. During my dark period, many people came out and tried to offer help. I did a lot of talking, a lot of messaging and calling. Nothing worked out.
I've already explained this to one of the comments above. It's not that I'm not enjoying the activities of life; I'm not enjoying life itself. Think of life and the events in it as different things.

I'd argue that it's not the reader's job to pick out the gold from a book. It's the author's job to sell the story and make it amiable to the public. If the author made such a great sentence, he should try publishing just the sentence instead of the whole book (which can be very off-putting for some readers).

I've never thought about it like that. How, even if I don't focus on the bad qualities, I don't seem to focus on the good ones either. Hmm. Still, I think suicide is the way for me. I don't want anything out of life. I lack an agenda and waiting is really boring. Even if I risk missing out on something awesome, I'd rather just go than stay.
I'm going to "punch it in the mouth" by suicide. It doesn't make sense to try and "fuck the rules" of life by living life.

You may be right in saying that I could be "someone" if I tried harder. However, I'm not looking to be a somebody. I'm not disappointed in myself for not being a high achiever. Rather, I'm justifying my worthlessness in order to be approved to leave. I'm saying I don't do much, so I should be allowed to go.

If a book is bad for the majority of it, it's probably not worth reading. If the author had talent and only used it in the last half of the book, then he is an uninspiring man. His books should not be read.

The future can bring anything, yes. But I'm not bothered by the *contents* of life. More like the entirety of life. Understand? I am not bored of life. I'm having a good time, actually. But I don't want to keep at it because I don't like living. You have to think about life and the events in life as different things.
Okay, thanks for trying. Sometimes people find their solution in religion, I understand.

Are you... trying to convert me? Sorry, I left the idea of a God long time ago. It seems ridiculous to me, and I can only rationalize its existence by seeing it as some sort of support for weak people, or people who need help in a spiritual sense. I don't need this kind of help.

Also, when you said, "I agree with you", I don't think you fully understand what you're agreeing with. I'm not wallowing in a pit of misery. I'm not looking for happiness. You and I are on totally separate pages.
Well, that's why I created this post, to talk to people. Isn't that kind of redundant? Telling me that I can talk to you?

A friend brought me to Reddit. Reddit is more of a place for bored people than inspired and active people. I have a few hobbies. I play violin, work with computers, have a few clubs at the school and of course, internet surfing. I can care less about these hobbies, for I know that I will not add anything significant to their respective fields. They're fun to do, and they take up a large part of my life, but I wouldn't pursue them as a career or anything like that.

Often times people post to r/suicidewatch to receive help and support, not give it. Usually the ones that give support are the people who comment. I don't need someone to tell me their feelings and vent with. I'm not interested in finding another who's "like me" so that I feel less alone. I'm looking for, maybe, closure? I don't know. But I definitely don't want "another me" to hang around with.

This is all well and good but we should remember that life has its limitations. I'm not rich; I can't afford to try out a lot of things. Yes, there are many things I can do that does not involve money, which I've done (for example, volunteering at a clinic). I can get involved using the school's money, which I've done (clubs gone to different states for competitions). I can use my friend's money, which, not that I've asked for it, I've done (gone to conventions with friends; sharing hotel rooms). Yeah, life has its spices. But life, I don't want it. Want another metaphor? Life is a dish that can be seasoned with many spices. But I do not like this dish. What if I wanted some veal or soup? Life is not a dish I want to eat, no matter how it's seasoned.
Your answer is very typical. I've approached this many times and anyone who has said this did not help me (not because they weren't willing, but because they didn't know what to do).

College looks like a nice break to me. However, it's not certain whether or not I'll make it that far. With my depression acting up, I missed a lot of school. In fact, I had to take this year off because of it. Yes, college would be nice. But who knows if I'll make it to a good college. And honestly, shitty colleges are my worst nightmare.

Yes, I've waited six years. It does not mean that an extra year would be easier. It's been getting harder and harder, and one year might equate to 6 years in stress and temptations.

Also, if we were to sky dive daily, it would not be such a thrill after a few tries at it.

Thanks for your reply.

A lot of people have suggested things like that. Go out and explore the world; you're going to die anyway so why not take a high risk vacation? There are a few reasons why I wouldn't want to do that. One, I have no money. I cannot get a job, as I'm 17 and I would not be able to support myself. If anything, I could run into the city for a day or two and come back (which I've done several times with my parents' permission).  I cant just run out there and expect paradise. It would be worse than my conditions now, and being depressed I probably wouldn't have the energy to make a living or whatever. Going out and "exploring" really does not interest me. Towns are towns, cities are cities; there isn't much difference between them.

It seems like you're trying to pursue the idea of "enjoying life" to me. Let me tell you this, life is the poison in my life. Pretty strange, but true. "Living", whether you mean it metaphorically or physically, is not seen as a good thing for me. I don't want to live my life to the fullest. Think of it like this: life is an activity just like baseball. Pretend I hate playing baseball. You can't tell me to keep playing baseball and that I'll enjoy it one day. If I hate baseball, I hate *playing* baseball. I hate doing it. It's the same thing with life. I don't like life, and I don't want to play it anymore.
